overview: This Senate resolution designates April 2026 as Second Chance Month. It focuses on "collateral consequences," the legal and social barriers people with criminal records often face after completing their sentences, such as trouble finding jobs, housing, professional licenses, education funding and access to capital. The findings note federal laws aimed at helping people re-enter society, including the Second Chance Act of 2007 and the First Step Act of 2018. The resolution honors groups working to remove unnecessary barriers and calls on Americans to observe the month by raising awareness and offering closure to people who have paid their debt to society. It is ceremonial and does not change any law. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on April 28, 2026.
for: Supporters say helping people who have served their sentences find work and housing reduces repeat crime and strengthens families and communities.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law, and some may question how it describes which barriers are unnecessary for public safety.
